title: Replicated Key-Value Store with Tunable Consistency
objective: Build a single-leader, multi-follower key-value store that runs as independent OS processes communicating only over the network, with a client-selectable read mode, and produce a reproducible demonstration of a real consistency anomaly that exists in one mode and not the other.
whyThisMatters: Consistency models stop being folklore the moment you can make an anomaly appear and disappear on demand in a system you built yourself. This task is the baseline the rest of the term measures itself against: every later task assumes you can say precisely what 'the leader acknowledged the write' does and does not guarantee.
evidence: Git history showing the leader-only version committed before followers and read modes were added
The reproduction script plus a captured run of its output showing the anomaly under relaxed mode and its absence under strict mode
README.md naming the consistency model each mode satisfies, tied to the demonstrated anomaly
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: The leader and at least two followers run as separate OS processes exchanging state only over a network socket protocol.
The reproduction script deterministically reproduces the stale/missing read every run under relaxed mode and never under strict mode.
README names a specific consistency model (linearizable, sequential, causal, or eventual) for each mode and ties the claim to the demonstrated anomaly, not to a general assertion.
The write path's acknowledgment semantics are stated explicitly (leader-only ack vs. quorum ack).
